steps.text: **Our archive.** [S] 215 games in our files (TWIC and Lichess broadcast PGNs, 2020 to 2026) reach the knight sacrifice on f7 and the king's recapture (the Alien move order). White won 95, Black won 106, and 14 were drawn. This lesson uses four White wins. [V] We chose wins that teach something, so these four are not typical: they show how White can win, not how often.
steps.chapter: How to read an archive game

steps.text: **Ratings matter more than the line.** [S] In the 212 games where both ratings are in the file, White was the higher-rated player in 91: White won 54, Black 29, 8 drawn. White was the lower-rated player in 121: White won 40, Black 75, 6 drawn. [I] The rating gap predicts the result; the opening does not obviously decide it.

steps.prompt: Out of the 121 games in which White was the lower-rated player, how many do you think White won? Guess a number, then see the count.

steps.text: **Four games, four jobs.** Dyulgerov v Firman shows the sacrifice on h6. Dyulgerov v Boruchovsky shows the same sacrifice on h6, reached by another move order, with a rook lift to g4 doing the work the queen did in game 1. Haug v Svane shows the knight fork on g6 and a late blunder. Sevian v Sourath shows the g4 push and the loose pawn on e6. [S] Players' ratings in the headings come from the archive file; we have no other source for them.

steps.prompt: Between those two positions the evaluation swung from a large Black advantage to a clear White one. Name one kind of mistake that could produce such a swing, and one habit that would protect Black from it.

steps.text: **Patterns across the games.** [S] Games 1 and 2 turn on the sacrifice on h6; game 4 shows Black's edge surviving the loss of e6, with White winning later. [I] The pawns on h6 and e6 are the weak points the gambit player aims at. steps.prompt: [H] The engine rated Black ahead at some point in all four games, yet White won all four. Name one reason a better position can be lost, then one thing you could do as Black to make these games harder for White.

Include (a) the sacrifice on h6 and why the count matters, (b) one decision where the loser had a better move, and (c) why the archive's results do not prove the opening is good or bad. Self-check afterwards: did you say when each idea works and when it fails, give a position a beginner could set up, and name one mistake to avoid? The app grades nothing.

steps.text:
**Recap.**
1. Archive scores mix the line with the player and the rating gap.
2. The count on h6 shows a pawn is lost; whether the sacrifice works depends on what the queen does next.
3. ...Bxe5 depends on what dxe5 attacks: in game 1 it hit the knight on f6 with Qh5+ ready and lost; in game 2 it was fine at move 12 but lost after ...Nf8 and Bxh6.
4. A won position can be given back in one move.
5. Check e6 before blocking the c8 bishop.

steps.prompt: Optional: play on as Black from Firman's position after 13.Ne5+. Try the move the engine prefers, ...Kg8, and see how the game changes.
